lesson_title: Four Ways to Shape a Melt
hook_text: A bag of plastic rice goes into a machine. A wheelie bin comes out sixty seconds later. Four machines, four kinds of thing.
clip_script: Recycled pellets become products by melting and shaping. Injection moulding squirts melt under huge pressure into a steel mould: crates, caps, bins, bumpers, solid and detailed, cheap per part only in big numbers because the mould costs millions. Blow moulding inflates a tube of melt inside a mould: bottles, drums, jerry cans. Extrusion pushes melt through a shaped hole, endless pipe, gutter, frame, film. Rotational moulding tumbles powder in a hot hollow mould: water tanks, canoes. Pick by shape and numbers. Then design so it comes out right: even walls or it sinks and warps, a slight taper so it slides out, no hooks that lock it in, rounded corners, ribs for stiffness. Look at the underside of a crate and you will see every rule.
visual_style: Whiteboard four machines each with a product icon; a crate underside with ribs; a tapered wall with a draft angle; a thick lump with a sink mark crossed out.
pacing: Injection, blow, extrusion, rotational, choose, four rules.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and turn over a plastic crate or bucket to find the draft, the ribs and the gate mark.
